evidence.conversion: Vicat softening sits a little above HDT at 0.45 MPa for amorphous polymers

rows: its own Vicat 70 °C + 5 °C: Vicat softening (a 10 N needle, 1 mm penetration) is reached at or above HDT at 0.45 MPa for an unfilled bar; the highest Vicat the material's own grades publish caps its unfilled heat deflection estimate softly (BVOH's estimate reached 158 °C against its own Vicat of 90 °C). No melting-point margin is applied below the melting point itself: PVDF publishes 158 °C, 12 °C under its melting point.

45 °C floor: Heat deflection is measured by heating a loaded bar from room temperature (ISO 75, ASTM D648). A bar soft enough to deflect near room temperature has no meaningful HDT, and no filament in the snapshot measures below 48 °C even at 1.8 MPa. A soft floor, so a PE or BVOH estimate cannot reach below freezing.

rows: As the basis for the material, we used PETG, well-known for its excellent mechanical properties, supplemented by adding 10% PTFE, commonly known as Teflon, with self-lubricating properties.

Thanks to the meticulous selection of components while reducing the coefficient of friction, the filament retains the ease of printing, interlayer adhesion, impact strength and thermal properties typical of PETG.
Ruby or hardened nozzle not necessary
This material is designed for applications requiring low friction, increased wear resistance, and mechanical durability.

Thanks to its PTFE content, Fiberlogy PETG+PTFE enables the printing of sliding parts, guides, gears, and other components subjected to low or moderate loads , which are characterized by minimal friction and a longer service life. At the same time, the material retains all the advantages of PET-G: ease of printing, high adhesion to the build plate, chemical resistance, and good impact strength .
Exact-product maker claim; no suitability PASS, design allowable or qualified service lifetime. Concentration, temperature, duration and specimen unstated unless the source specifies them.

polymer.basis: Classification and typical values from polymer handbooks and resin data sheets, as compiled for the estimate model (docs/audits/2026-09-15-filtering-estimates-data/physics/). The document cited prints a density inside the range, not its ends. Eastman's data sheet for Eastar copolyester 6763 (R-EASTMAN-EASTAR-6763-TDS, a web page) prints, for injection-moulded bars, a specific gravity of 1.27 (ASTM D792) and a density of 1.27 g/cm³ (ISO 1183, method D), a water absorption of 0.13 % after 24 h immersion (ASTM D570 and ISO 62) and a glass transition temperature of 80 °C by DSC. It prints no saturation figure. Eastman's technical information for the grade (R-EASTMAN-EASTAR-6763-MBS80, MBS-80Q, SHA-256 f764fce37683...) calls it "a clear amorphous polymer" based "on poly(ethylene terephthalate)" (p. 3): the amorphous PET copolyester this row stands for.
